articles.title: Risk Factors for instability and dislocation after reverse total shoulder arthroplasty: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Ulenberg N, Herbstreit S, Dudda M, Vogel C, Mester B
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: Ten retrospective studies (six cohort studies, four case series)
articles.outcomes: Risk factors for postoperative instability or dislocation; mechanisms of instability classified by Frankle classification
articles.take_home: Eleven risk factors for instability after reverse shoulder replacement were identified, including male sex, younger age, opioid use disorder, depression, revision surgery, and certain implant choices. Loss of compression was the most common reason for instability, though researchers note these findings are based on older studies and may not prove these factors directly cause instability.

articles.title: Modified Partial Radial to Axillary Nerve Transfer as the Index Procedure for Isolated Axillary Nerve Injury.
articles.authors: Gupta R, Johnston TR, Lee C, Chen VY, Gonzales LP, Steward O
articles.population: Patients with isolated axillary nerve injury treated with partial radial-to-axillary nerve transfer
articles.outcomes: Muscle strength (MRC score improved by average 2.82 points), shoulder range of motion (forward flexion improved by average 108 degrees, abduction by 95 degrees, external rotation by 37 degrees), donor-site morbidity, and motor endplate survival in denervated muscle
articles.take_home: Partial radial-to-axillary nerve transfer significantly improved shoulder strength and movement in patients with axillary nerve injury, with benefits seen even when surgery was delayed beyond 6 months and without causing harm to the donor nerve site.

articles.title: The biomechanics of the sternoclavicular joint: an experimental and computational study.
articles.authors: Irshad TB, Pascoletti G, Zanetti EM
articles.outcomes: Range of motion of the sternoclavicular joint (elevation, retraction) and joint forces; validation of musculoskeletal model (OpenSim) against experimental data
articles.take_home: Researchers created a computer model of the sternoclavicular joint and tested it using movement sensors on people, finding the model reliably measures joint forces and upward clavicle movement but is less accurate for backward movement due to skin motion affecting the sensors.

articles.title: Outcomes of Implant Removal After Failed Radial Head Arthroplasty:An Average 7-Year Follow-up Study.
articles.authors: Hart CM, Weir TB, O'Driscoll CM, Esper R, Barlow JD, Yuan BJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients who had removal of a failed radial head implant without replacement, mean age 50 years
articles.outcomes: Patient satisfaction (Satisfaction or Dissatisfaction score), pain improvement, range of motion, complications including proximal radioulnar impingement
articles.take_home: Removing a failed radial head implant appears to be a reasonable option, with 84% of patients reporting their elbow was improved or better at 7-year follow-up. Three-quarters of patients with painful loose implants experienced improvement in forearm pain after removal.

articles.title: Risk of Shoulder/Elbow Injuries and Imaging Abnormalities in Female Collegiate Baseball and Softball Players.
articles.authors: Tsukahara Y, Jyoto E, Sato R
articles.population: Female collegiate baseball and softball players at national-level teams
articles.outcomes: Self-reported shoulder and elbow pain or discomfort; ultrasound findings of structural abnormalities in shoulder and elbow
articles.take_home: Most female collegiate overhead-throwing players showed abnormal ultrasound findings in their shoulders and elbows, with many reporting pain. Playing baseball before high school was linked to a much higher risk of elbow imaging abnormalities and shoulder pain, but early softball participation was not.

articles.title: Clinical impact of scapular stress fracture after reverse total shoulder arthroplasty: a single-center propensity score-matched analysis.
articles.authors: Chul-Hyun Cho B, Sohn HJ, Kim DH
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort comparison with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 28 patients with scapular stress fracture and 84 matched controls
articles.outcomes: Pain (VAS), function (UCLA, ASES, SSV scores), range of motion (forward flexion and abduction)
articles.take_home: Scapular stress fracture occurred in about 5% of reverse shoulder replacements and was associated with reduced shoulder movement (less lifting forwards and to the side) compared to those without fracture, though pain and overall satisfaction were similar. The location of the fracture affected how much movement patients regained, but whether the fracture was treated with surgery or not did not make a significant difference to the final outcome.

articles.title: The impact of glenoid polyethylene type, humeral head size and composition on revision risk following primary anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty for osteoarthritis.
articles.authors: Gill DRJ, Corfield S, McCau M, Blakeney WG
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national arthroplasty registry
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 10,431 procedures (4,797 with XLPE glenoids, 5,634 with non-XLPE glenoids)
articles.outcomes: Cumulative percent revision at 15 years, revision risk stratified by polyethylene type, humeral head size and material
articles.take_home: Highly cross-linked polyethylene glenoid components reduced the need for revision surgery compared to standard polyethylene, with a 15-year revision rate of 6.0% versus 11.4%. The benefit of the newer polyethylene was most apparent with medium-sized humeral heads and appeared less important with very small or very large head sizes.

articles.title: Gartner Type and Outcomes After US PAL Versus Arthroscopic Debridement for Calcific Tendinitis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Mi Y, Jiang B, Pan S, Jia X, Hu Y
articles.population: Patients with refractory calcific tendinitis of the shoulder
articles.sample_size: 72 patients (35 per group after propensity score matching)
articles.outcomes: Visual Analog Scale pain score, American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, and Constant-Murley score at baseline and 12 months
articles.take_home: Both ultrasound-guided aspiration and lavage and arthroscopic debridement improved symptoms, but the best treatment depends on calcification type. Arthroscopic debridement worked better for Type I calcifications, whilst ultrasound-guided aspiration and lavage worked as well as arthroscopic debridement for Type II calcifications and was quicker and cheaper.

articles.title: Association between shoulder pain, muscle strength, and closed kinetic chain performance tests in swimming athletes: Cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Dos Santos GA, Dos Santos ML, Solon-Junior LJF, Barbosa GM, de Araujo DLF, Santana SDF, et al.
articles.population: Competitive swimmers aged 12-60 years, including those with and without shoulder pain
articles.outcomes: Performance on modified Closed Kinetic Chain Upper Extremity Stability Test, Upper Quarter Y Balance Test, and Upper Limb Rotation Test, and association with shoulder pain and muscle strength measurements
articles.take_home: Shoulder pain and weakness in muscles throughout the kinetic chain, particularly in the hips, knees, and shoulder blade area, were associated with reduced performance on swimming stability and movement tests. These findings suggest that assessing and potentially strengthening the whole kinetic chain may be important for swimmers with shoulder problems.

articles.title: The Impact of Lesser Tuberosity Osteotomy Repair After Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Aleem AW, Zmistowski BM, Sefko J, Chen L, Keener JD
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty with an intact subscapularis tendon suitable for reattachment
articles.outcomes: American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) score, internal rotation range of motion, internal rotation functional score, other active shoulder motions
articles.take_home: Repairing the lesser tuberosity bone fragment to reattach the subscapularis tendon during reverse shoulder replacement led to better functional scores and improved internal rotation movement at 2 years, without affecting movement in other directions.

articles.title: Pre-operative biopsies in the revision setting - helpful or harmful?
articles.authors: Howard M, Thomas W, Evans J, Kitson J, Smith C
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision shoulder or elbow procedures for presumed aseptic (non-infected) cases
articles.outcomes: Detection of infection by pre-operative biopsy compared to intra-operative findings; sensitivity of pre-operative biopsy; rates of newly identified infection at revision
articles.take_home: Pre-operative biopsies to check for infection before revision surgery have low sensitivity (54%) and may not be helpful, as they miss infections and can introduce new infections. Taking biopsies at the time of the actual revision surgery appears to be more reliable for identifying infections that need treatment.

articles.title: Semi-inlay and onlay humeral stems in reverse shoulder arthroplasty achieve comparable outcomes through different patterns of glenoid and humeral lateralization and distalization: A retrospective study from the FP-UCBM Shoulder Study Group.
articles.authors: Paciotti M, De Rosa A, Franceschetti E, La Bruna M, Gregori P, Ciuffreda M, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary reverse shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 164 patients (41 semi-inlay; 123 onlay) at mean follow-up of 28 months
articles.outcomes: Constant-Murley Score, Simple Shoulder Test, Visual Analog Scale, range of motion, radiographic measurements of glenoid and humeral positioning, scapular notching incidence
articles.take_home: Two different types of reverse shoulder replacement stem design achieved equally good clinical results, but they positioned the shoulder joint components in different ways. The study suggests that what matters for success is achieving the right overall positioning, regardless of which stem type is used.

articles.title: Management of the dislocated reverse total shoulder arthroplasty: A tertiary centre experience.
articles.authors: Asaad O, Raval P, Raja H, Falworth M, Rudge W, Majed A, et al.
articles.population: Patients with dislocated reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Stability achievement rate, revision procedure type, persistence of instability
articles.take_home: Most dislocations after reverse shoulder replacement happen within 6 weeks and are caused by loss of compression around the joint. Surgery to replace the modular components was successful in restoring stability in about half the cases, though some patients needed more extensive surgery.
